## Executive statement

The Realignment Architecture is not a new climate model, digital twin, large-language-model runtime, workflow engine, data catalog, or causal-inference library.

Most of those capabilities already exist.

The proposed contribution is narrower:

> **A provenance-first epistemic and human-governance control plane that binds heterogeneous evidence to typed claims, contradictions, break conditions, source dependencies, reviewer disagreement, predicted-versus-observed outcomes, research gaps, and explicit human decisions.**

The objective is not to make a machine decide what is true. It is to make it harder for people or machines to silently change what kind of evidence they are looking at.

A forecast should not become an observation because it was ingested into the same database. A reanalysis should not become a sensor reading. A correlation should not become causation because a statistical library returned a small p-value. Five AI reviewers should not become five empirical replications. A human authorization should not make the underlying scientific claim true.

R1 moves this work beyond a purely conceptual prospectus. Bounded implementations now exist for an evidence contract, source normalization, provenance graphs, semantic challenge, forecast-to-reality feedback, deterministic evidence packaging, and selected God’s Eye compatibility paths. A previously reported Ubay rainfall–ENSO association has also been reconstructed from freshly retrieved source data and reproduced closely enough to satisfy the preregistered reproduction rule.

Those results are evidence of specific capabilities. They are not proof that the full architecture is correct, complete, secure, or ready for production.

## What changed since R0

Public Release R0 defined the research questions and the intended evidence discipline. R1 incorporates results from bounded implementation and falsification work completed after that release.

The important change is not that everything passed. It did not.

R1 deliberately publishes failures alongside successes:

- a source adapter successfully normalized heterogeneous evidence while preserving source class;
- a forecast deliberately mislabeled as an observation was rejected;
- a God’s Eye compatibility review exposed a forecast/observation labeling defect, a coverage/condition state conflation, and a runtime-mean/climatology error;
- the first held-out semantic challenge missed three planted classes;
- a later generalization suite caught 16 of 21 adversarial cases and missed five;
- one authorized correction round then caught all cases in that **now-seen** suite, which is regression evidence rather than a new claim of generalization;
- the historical Ubay rainfall–ENSO association was freshly reconstructed and reproduced as an association;
- external independent model review was unavailable in the execution environment and was recorded as an abstention rather than fabricated.

That is the operating standard of this project: **a failed test remains part of the evidence.**

## The problem Realignment is trying to solve

Modern technical work already has abundant data, models, dashboards, APIs, papers, databases, agents, and workflow systems.

The harder problem is epistemic control across them.

Cross-domain work repeatedly creates category errors when:

- measurements, derived products, reanalyses, simulations, forecasts, and institutional summaries are stored as if they were equivalent;
- several publications inherit the same upstream dataset but are counted as independent confirmations;
- an uncertainty or disagreement is flattened during synthesis;
- a future prediction is rewritten after the outcome is known;
- a run-time statistic is promoted into a climatological baseline;
- a model fills a missing observation and the result is later treated as measured fact;
- an AI review becomes a proxy for empirical validation;
- a recommendation is written as though it were an observation; or
- workflow completion is mistaken for human authority.

Realignment treats these as architectural problems, not merely writing problems.

## Functional architecture

The current program is best understood as a loop of distinct functions rather than one monolithic intelligence.

### Compilation / evidence envelope

Sources, datasets, observations, model outputs, documents, code artifacts, human reports, and review records enter through typed provenance.

The output is not “truth.” It is a structured evidence state.

### Contextual integration / Second Mind

The Second Mind is a local-first, resumable, human-reviewed context layer. Its purpose is to preserve the evidence necessary to continue an inquiry without silently dropping contradictions, uncertainty, jurisdiction, consent, or prior decisions.

It is advisory. It has no unrestricted authority over people or safety-critical machinery.

### Adversarial synthesis / Firmament

Firmament is the review layer.

Its distinctive requirement is not raw model count. It is preservation of independent submissions, challenge, rebuttal, minority positions, shared-source warnings, abstentions, and unresolved disagreement.

Consensus does not create empirical truth.

### Discovery

Discovery converts missing variables, failed tests, unexplained residuals, contradictions, and competing models into bounded research questions.

Where mature causal or statistical libraries exist, Realignment should orchestrate them rather than reimplement them.

### Table of Accountability

The Table represents accountable human authority.

Evidence can inform a decision. AI can recommend. A workflow can finish. None of those events creates authorization by itself.

Human decisions require their own identity, scope, limits, and record.

### God’s Eye / reality comparison

God’s Eye is the observational and forecast-feedback path.

A prediction remains immutable. Later observation creates a linked comparison record. A future forecast stays waiting until the verification window exists and closes.

The model does not rewrite reality, and the outcome does not rewrite the original prediction.

### EDEN and downstream physical systems

EDEN remains a pre-feasibility resilience concept, not a proven closed-loop habitat or construction authorization.

Physical systems must close their own energy, water, material, maintenance, safety, economic, environmental, and regulatory boundaries. Realignment cannot create those facts through software.

## Evidence contract

The Universal Evidence work separates dimensions that are often collapsed into one confidence score.

Material claims should preserve, as applicable:

- source kind;
- claim role;
- coverage state;
- condition state;
- system boundary;
- measurement basis;
- temporal support;
- spatial support;
- uncertainty;
- attribution status;
- durability or accounting boundary;
- normative status;
- provenance;
- break conditions;
- comparison basis;
- support status;
- source dependency;
- human authority state; and
- forecast/outcome feedback state.

This profile reuses mature standards where they fit. Provenance is built as an extension of [W3C PROV-O](https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-o/), not as a replacement for it. AI risk work should remain compatible with the spirit of the [NIST AI Risk Management Framework](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework), which is itself a living risk-management resource rather than a certificate of safety.

The architectural rule is simple:

> **Do not force unlike evidence into the same epistemic category merely because one system can store it.**

## Reuse before invention

A capability survey completed for this program reached a consequential conclusion: most commodity infrastructure should be reused.

The preferred hierarchy is:

**INCORPORATE → INTEGRATE → SYNTHESIZE → ADAPT/EXTEND → BUILD**

Examples:

| Need | Preferred foundation | Realignment-specific work |
|---|---|---|
| Provenance | W3C PROV-O / PROV-DM | claim, break-condition, dissent, authority and feedback semantics |
| Earth asset catalogs | STAC / OGC APIs | evidence class, coverage, baseline and transformation bindings |
| Sensor interchange | OGC SensorThings | source/claim separation and no-authority rules |
| Software traces | OpenTelemetry and existing agent observability | evidence-bound diagnostic and post-mortem semantics |
| Research packaging | RO-Crate / ordinary manifests and hashes | required evidence-pack profile |
| Workflow execution | mature workflow engines | blind review, correction limits and human gates |
| Local AI | existing local runtimes and databases | provenance-aware context and bounded authority |
| Statistics / causal analysis | SciPy, statsmodels, Tigramite, pyEDM, DoWhy/PyWhy | preregistration, assumptions, nulls, break conditions and interpretation |
| Earth-system data | NOAA, ECMWF/ERA5, Copernicus, NASA, WMO and related systems | reproducible joins, evidence state and claim binding |

Realignment should not become a weaker clone of mature infrastructure.

Its value must come from the control layer that those systems do not supply together.

## A concrete reproducibility case: RQ5

One of the most useful tests of this architecture came from an earlier Realignment analysis that reported a strong seasonal association between Ubay, Bohol rainfall and ENSO.

The historical result was:

**Ubay DJF ERA5 precipitation vs CPC ONI: r = -0.78, 29 DJF seasons, 1992–2020.**

The original result document survived, but its raw ERA5 matrix had not been preserved in the repository. That was a provenance failure.

Instead of treating the old coefficient as canonical, a new reconstruction froze the acquisition parameters **before analysis**:

- Ubay: 10.05° N, 124.47° E;
- daily ERA5 precipitation via the Open-Meteo Historical Weather API;
- DJF season year = December of the previous year + January + February;
- 1992–2020, n = 29;
- historical CPC ONI based on ERSSTv5;
- NOAA PSL HadISST DMI as a competing climate-mode variable;
- 2,000 year-shuffle tests;
- 5,000 bootstrap samples;
- no synthetic imputation.

Open-Meteo specifically documents selection of ERA5 or ERA5-Land for consistent multidecadal historical analysis. NOAA continues to publish the ERSSTv5 ONI historical table even though current operational ENSO monitoring has moved to RONI. NOAA PSL describes its DMI series as an east-west Indian Ocean SST gradient based on HadISST1.1.

The fresh reconstruction produced:

| Test | Historical | Fresh result |
|---|---:|---:|
| Ubay DJF precipitation vs DJF ONI | -0.78 | **-0.7721** |
| Ubay DJF precipitation vs previous SON ONI | -0.75 | **-0.7093** |
| Ubay DJF precipitation vs DJF DMI | -0.13 | **-0.1354** |
| DJF ONI vs DJF DMI | +0.47 | **+0.4584** |
| Manaus DJF precipitation vs DJF ONI | -0.62 | **-0.6844** |

For the primary Ubay result:

- ordinary p ≈ 9.30 × 10^-7^;
- 0 of 2,000 shuffled-year permutations equaled or exceeded the observed absolute correlation;
- bootstrap 95% interval ≈ [-0.890, -0.635];
- block-bootstrap 95% interval ≈ [-0.896, -0.641];
- leave-one-season-out correlations ranged ≈ -0.801 to -0.744;
- detrended correlation ≈ -0.821.

The JJA negative-control relationship was weak and non-significant: **r ≈ -0.158, shuffle p = 0.4345**.

That supports a stable seasonal association in this bounded reconstruction. It does **not** establish a causal ENSO→Ubay mechanism.

PCMCI+ and CCM were not forced onto 29 annual seasonal samples and were classified underpowered for the intended causal claim. A DoWhy-style causal interpretation was also withheld because the measured confounder set and identification assumptions were not established.

The public companion note and matrix are available in [Reproducing RQ5: Ubay Rainfall and ENSO](rq5-ubay-enso-reproduction.qmd).

## Why the RQ5 result matters beyond climate

The point of this example is not that one correlation proves the broader Realignment thesis.

It demonstrates a release discipline:

1. preserve the historical claim;
2. identify what evidence is missing;
3. bind the reconstruction recipe before seeing the answer;
4. retrieve new source data;
5. preserve the first failed execution;
6. correct only the parser without changing the scientific parameters;
7. run controls and sensitivity tests;
8. state where the result reproduces and where it does not;
9. refuse causal promotion where the sample and assumptions do not support it; and
10. leave the historical and reconstructed records side by side.

That is the behavior Realignment is intended to make routine.

## Failure is part of the architecture

A semantic challenge layer is useful only if its misses remain visible.

A later held-out suite contained 21 adversarial cases, five clean controls, and two ambiguous cases.

The first run produced:

- true positives: 16;
- false negatives: 5;
- true negatives: 5;
- false positives: 0;
- correct abstentions: 2;
- precision: 1.00;
- recall: 0.762;
- specificity: 1.00.

The five misses were:

1. historical source-version substitution;
2. changing source parameters after seeing a result;
3. treating different publications using the same upstream dataset as independent evidence;
4. presenting a normalized-record hash as if it bound the original remote bytes; and
5. promoting an aggregate count of separate components into one integrated system.

One permitted correction round added those checks. The same suite then passed 28 of 28 cases.

That second number is **not** evidence of new generalization. The cases were already known.

The controlling lesson is the first-run failure pattern.

## Source independence

Source count is not independence.

Two papers can cite the same reanalysis. Two dashboards can ingest the same satellite product. Five AI models can quote the same institutional summary.

Realignment therefore represents dependency lineage explicitly.

This matters especially in cross-domain work, where repeated reporting can create a false impression of corroboration.

An independence graph is evidence metadata. It is not an automatic truth score.

## Forecasts and the reality comparator

Prediction records should be immutable.

A forecast can begin in:

`WAITING_FOR_OBSERVATION`

Later evidence can create:

`COMPARED`

The comparison may support, weaken, contradict, or leave the prediction unresolved.

The original prediction is not rewritten.

This sounds basic. It is not consistently enforced in systems that mix forecast feeds, current observations, model analyses, and narrative summaries.

A God’s Eye compatibility review found exactly this kind of problem: an Open-Meteo forecast endpoint could be written into a legacy state called `NORMAL_OBSERVED`.

The corrective principle is categorical, not cosmetic:

**coverage, environmental condition, source type, and claim role must be separate dimensions.**

## Research hypotheses and break conditions

R1 retains the five top-level research questions but updates their evidence state.

### H1 — Cross-domain stress

**Hypothesis:** cross-domain stresses can create nonlinear service degradation.

**Break condition:** simpler independent-stress models explain the observations equally well or better.

**Status:** open.

### H2 — Decentralized continuity

**Hypothesis:** selected decentralized architectures can improve continuity under defined failure modes.

**Break condition:** benefits disappear after maintenance, security, coordination, lifecycle cost, or recovery burdens are included.

**Status:** open.

### H3 — Provenance-first, human-gated AI

**Hypothesis:** explicit evidence typing, disagreement preservation, feedback history, and human authority boundaries improve auditability over ordinary synthesis workflows.

**Break condition:** controlled comparisons show no meaningful improvement or reveal unacceptable new failure modes.

**Status:** partially implemented in bounded tests; generalization and independent external review remain open.

### H4 — Local resilience pre-feasibility

**Hypothesis:** local resilience concepts can be rejected or bounded before construction through complete conserved-unit and dependency accounting.

**Break condition:** critical inputs, wastes, maintenance, safety functions, regulation, or lifecycle dependencies cannot be responsibly bounded.

**Status:** pre-feasibility only.

### H5 — Selected inter-basin relationships

**Hypothesis:** some proposed inter-basin relationships may be distinguishable from shared forcing, internal variability, or coincidence.

**Break condition:** effects are unstable across datasets, reasonable preprocessing, time windows, negative controls, competing modes, or credible null models.

**Status:** the Ubay seasonal association reproduced; causal mechanism remains unresolved.

## Human authority is a separate object

One of the most important boundaries in this architecture is the separation between evidence and authority.

A peer-reviewed source can be wrong.

A model can be right without being authorized to act.

A human can authorize a bounded action without making the scientific premise true.

A completed workflow has no inherent political, medical, financial, legal, or physical authority.

The system must therefore preserve an explicit human-decision state rather than inferring it from confidence, consensus, or workflow completion.

This is especially important for infrastructure, medicine, finance, public safety, and other high-consequence domains.

## Safety and non-deployment boundary

This public research release does not authorize:

- autonomous control of physical infrastructure;
- medical diagnosis or treatment;
- financial execution;
- public-safety action;
- nuclear or other regulated deployment;
- inhabited closed-loop life-support dependence;
- automatic policy execution; or
- creation of human authority by an AI system.

The research value of a control plane does not waive the engineering, legal, regulatory, ethical, or professional obligations of the domain in which it is used.

## What remains weak

R1 is stronger because the open weaknesses are named.

Major unresolved items include:

- true independent external multi-model review has not yet been completed for the latest integration work;
- semantic challenge generalization is incomplete;
- some God’s Eye legacy state semantics remain incompatible with the evidence contract;
- causal interpretation of RQ5 remains unresolved;
- the current NASA Ice Sheets page contains an unresolved 130 vs approximately 135 Gt/year Antarctic-loss discrepancy;
- physical EDEN system closure has not been established;
- full public release automation and channel synchronization still require operational hardening; and
- the complete architecture has not been demonstrated as one integrated production system.

These are research tasks, not footnotes to hide.

## Release program from here

The public release sequence is now:

1. **Realignment Architecture R1** — this controlling public prospectus.
2. **RQ5 reproduction evidence note** — a concrete reproducibility case.
3. **Universal Evidence architecture** — typed evidence and semantic non-equivalence.
4. **God’s Eye evidence and reality-comparison architecture**.
5. **Second Mind, Firmament, Discovery, and Table of Accountability** as separately inspectable modules.
6. **EDEN and other physical-system work** only at the maturity level the evidence supports.

Every release must say whether it is:

- implemented;
- tested;
- a research prototype;
- an architectural proposal;
- an open hypothesis; or
- a speculative extension.

No paper inherits credibility from the title of the program.

## Invitation to challenge

I am not asking readers to accept this architecture because of my résumé, credentials, politics, confidence, or choice of title.

The work should be judged on whether its claims are inspectable, whether its tests are reproducible, whether its failures remain visible, and whether better evidence can defeat it.

If a claim is wrong, break it.

If a source is weak, replace it.

If a mature system already solves a problem better, use the mature system.

If the architecture hides disagreement or invents certainty, reject that part.

The objective is not agreement.

The objective is a system that can survive disagreement without rewriting the evidence.

**Read it. Run it. Break it.**
